facts: $|x|$ is the distance of $x$ from $0$ on a number line, so $|x| \ge 0$ for all real numbers.
Opposite numbers have equal absolute value: $|-x| = |x|$ for all real numbers $x$.
The distance between two numbers $a$ and $b$ on a number line is $|a - b| = |b - a|$.
Power property: $|a|^2 = a^2$ for all real numbers $a$.
The **triangle inequality** states that $|a + b| \le |a| + |b|$ for all real numbers $a$ and $b$.

mastery.question_text: Simplify $\dfrac{|-2x^3|}{|x|}$ for any non-zero real number $x$.

The coordinates of points $P, Q, R$ on a number line are $-7, 1, 9$ respectively.
Determine whether the distance between $P$ and $R$ equals the sum of the distances from $P$ to $Q$ and $Q$ to $R$.
mastery.solution_text:
PQ = |1 - (-7)| = |8| = 8
QR = |9 - 1| = |8| = 8
PR = |9 - (-7)| = |16| = 16
PQ + QR = 8 + 8 = 16 = PR
$\text{Yes, the distance between } P \text{ and } R \text{ equals } PQ + QR = 16.$
